full_judgment: 11. Mrs Shimonti Ahmed, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of respondents Nos. 1-6 in Writ Petition No. 10279 of 2017 contends that in view of the admitted fact that on the basis of the resolution dated 12-7-2017 taken by all the 31 (thirty one) teachers of the Economics Department a complaint was lodged to the Vice-Chancellor of the University intimating that unless an appropriate action was taken against the petitioner, they would all abstain from taking any class of the Department. The Vice-Chancellor placed the resolution of the Department before the Syndicate meeting and upon considering facts and circumstances of the case and the previous record of the petitioner, the Syndicate rightly took the decision to send the petitioner on forced leave on 12-7-2017. Mrs. Ahmed further contends that the Syndicate took the decision in accordance with the provisions of Article 24(k) of the Dhaka University Order, 1973 and not under the provision of Chapter-XIX, Regulation 16 of the Dhaka University Ordinance and Regulation, 1997. The learned Advocate further contends that the provisions as provided in Chapter XIX, Regulation 16 of the Dhaka University Ordinance and Regulation, 1997 empower the Vice-Chancellor of the University to require any teacher/staff to go on leave for a period not exceeding 3 (three) months, but when the Syndicate takes any such step against any teacher/staff of the University under the provision of Article 24(k) of the Dhaka University Order, 1973, it has got no limitation of time. In the instant case, the decision to send the petitioner on forced leave was taken considering the unanimous resolution of the teachers of the Economics Department for avoiding any disruption of any peaceful academic atmosphere of the Department. As such, there is no illegality on the part of the Syndicate in taking the decision of forced leave and therefore, the question of declaring the same as illegal does not arise at all.
